subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the principle of production of electromagnetic waves?

mark_split.label: The changing fields produce each other

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: electromagnetic waves are radiated by an accelerating or oscillating charge (a charge at rest or in uniform motion radiates nothing); the wave sustains itself because a changing electric field produces a changing magnetic field and a changing magnetic field produces a changing electric field — both directions of the exchange stated, as the book prints (p.41).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The source: an accelerating charge
lines: Electromagnetic waves are produced by an
steps.margin_note: First mark. A charge at rest or in uniform motion radiates no wave.
steps.why: A charge at rest gives only a steady electric field, and a charge in uniform motion gives steady fields. Only an accelerating charge makes the changing fields a wave needs.
common_mistakes: Writing that any moving charge radiates. A charge moving with constant velocity does not; it must accelerate or oscillate.
Naming a steady current as the source. A steady current radiates nothing; the current must change with time.

recall.must_convey: That an accelerating or oscillating charge produces electromagnetic waves.

steps.memory_tip: No acceleration, no wave — an oscillating charge accelerates all the time.

steps.label: The two changing fields
steps.mark_note: Changing E and B produce each other
lines: A changing electric field produces a
changing magnetic field, and a changing
electric field. The two fields keep
producing each other, and this pair
travels through space as the wave.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. State both directions of the effect — E to B and B to E.
steps.why: One direction alone is not a wave. The wave keeps itself going because each changing field creates the other, so both statements are needed.
common_mistakes: Writing only that a changing magnetic field produces an electric field. The reverse statement is equally part of the principle.
Saying the electric field produces the magnetic field. It is the change in each field that produces the other.

recall.must_convey: That a changing electric field produces a changing magnetic field and a changing magnetic field produces a changing electric field.
accept: changing electric field produces magnetic field
changing magnetic field produces electric field
the two fields produce each other

steps.memory_tip: Two mirror sentences: E changing makes B, B changing makes E.

insider_note: Write both halves of the exchange — E to B and B to E; a one-direction answer reads as half the principle.
